text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian Moslem-Croat Federation army will consist of four corps according to decision by Moslem chairman of collective Bosnian Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and Federation President Kresimir Zubak, Bosnian army says.

- Moslem reporters abused and threatened with arms by Bosnian Croat man while waiting for results from a joint meeting of top city officials held in office of regional High Representative in Croat-run part of divided town of Mostar.
- Moslem teenager wounded in leg by bullet most probably was fired from Croat-controlled Mostar, Bosnian police report.

- Former prime minister of Spain, Felipe Gonzales, packing up bags and heading for Sarajevo to replace Swedish colleague Carl Bildt, current international High Representative for Bosnia, thE daily quotes diplomatic sources as saying.
- Croatia spends 100 million German marks to support Bosnian Croat self-styled republic of Herceg Bosna, political sources tell the newspaper.

- A meeting between Moslem-Croat Federation ministers and expelled Moslem authorities from disputed north Bosnian town of Brcko focused on news that Bosnian Serbs from Brcko are being given arms by their authorities.
- According to state-controlled commission for missing persons, 31 mass graves and hundreds of single graves were discovered in 1996 with 1,928 Moslems and Croats as victims.
- Bosnia's Serb republic is not state but entity inside Bosnia, a leader of its opposition Independent Social Democrats, Milorad Dodik, says in interview.
